impl:B-fine-register.deviations_from_spec: (1) Backward problem of V5 uses FineDense with the FORWARD stage's similarity (dense global 'ncc' when the forward used ncc, lcc2 when mixed) rather than lcc, so ICE measures inverse consistency of the same loss instead of mixing in LCC-vs-NCC disagreement; FineDense therefore also implements sim='ncc'. (2) FineDense reuses Refiner.refine through subclassing (identical parametrisation, cosine schedule, relative clamps, best-loss kept) instead of a separately copied Adam loop. (3) Polarity guard thresholds follow spec 2.4 (0.60/0.40 with |mean| >= 0.05), not the 65 % of the P2 recipe quoted in the task text. (4) erode_ball pads the mask with one zero voxel before the EDT so array faces erode like P2's binary_erosion (spec formula otherwise unchanged). (5) Gate (d) is generalised to ceil(0.625 n) converged restarts (= 5 of 8) and skipped when --fine-restarts 0; restart p95 is the pooled p95 over all converged (restart, point) pairs. (6) FineConfig has two extra non-flag fields (rigid_iters=150, n_points=50000) so test_fine.py can shorten the rigid stage; register.py never exposes them (v1 call sequence untouched). (7) The vascular restarts are compared against T_vasc (the vascular solution) also when the gate rejects it, keeping G3's n_within_0.3mm comparable to v1; vs_structural remains the candidate's move. (8) 'V_oct_mask_cm3' in prep_summary is prep.json's V_oct_cm3_tex when mask_mode == texture, else V_oct_cm3_int (None on legacy preps). (9) Level skip reason 'specimen_mask_too_small' (< 1000 voxels) added beside 'mixed_polarity'. (10) The two remaining CPU tests (iters 5 verification, iters 60 optimisation) had not finished when this report was forced; their numbers are not claimed.

findings.claim: destripe_inplace writes each chunk's core back into `vol` while later chunks still read their +-pad slices from `vol`; this is only correct when the reads come from forked workers that see the pre-fork copy-on-write pages. In the serial fallback (n_workers <= 1, no 'fork' start method, or len(jobs) == 1 with more chunks) and whenever `vol` is a shared (r+) memmap, chunk k+1's padding contains the already-destriped core of chunk k, so the normalised-convolution flat field is estimated from partly corrected data and the result is silently wrong (double correction near every chunk start).
findings.evidence: Local synthetic test (90x70x200 f16, x-stripes period 7.5, sigma 12/12/6 vox, zchunk 32, pad 40): n_workers=2 (fork) == P3 whole-volume formula bit-for-bit (0 differing voxels); n_workers=1 -> 730,246 of 1,260,000 voxels differ, max |diff| 1,760 intensity units (stripe amplitude 2,500), all differing z-slices lie in chunks 2-3 (z 32..89) i.e. after the first write-back; single-chunk serial == reference. r+ memmap input with Pool(2) -> 817,299 voxels differ. The serial path is reachable from the public API (test_destripe.py --n-workers, default 4) and on platforms without fork; production prep_subject.py (ndarray octv, n_workers=4, Linux) takes the correct path, consistent with owner C's NCC 1.00000 vs P3 on I58.
findings.fix: Never read padding from the array being modified: either collect all cores and write them back after the loop (`results = [...]; for c0,c1,core,_ in results: vol[...] = core`), or in the serial path snapshot the needed pad slices before overwriting; additionally refuse/copy `np.memmap` inputs (`if isinstance(vol, np.memmap): raise/ copy`) since the fork trick does not protect shared file mappings.
